questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.**

You are __so efficient as he__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **as efficient as he is**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "You are as efficient as he is." is a grammatically correct comparative sentence, and its correctness can be explained based on comparative structures, subject pronouns, and parallelism in sentence construction.
 
• Comparative Structure Using "as...as"
 
 
• In English grammar, when making comparisons of equality, we use the structure:
 
• **as + adjective/adverb + as + noun/pronoun**
 
 
 
• In this case, the **adjective** "efficient" is used to compare the efficiency of **"you" **and **"he."**
 
• Example:
 
 
• "You are as charming as he is."
 
 
 
• The Role of **"he"** as a **Subject Pronoun**
 
 
• Here, "he" is a subject pronoun that refers to the full clause "he is efficient."
 
 
 
• The Role of **"is" **in **Parallel Structure**
 
 
• To maintain parallelism, the second part of the sentence should mirror the first part. The verb** "is" **is necessary to complete the comparison clearly.
 
• "You are as efficient as he is (efficient)."
 
 

​Hence, the correct answer is: **as efficient as he is**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Why not "him" in place of 'he'?**

 
 
• **​**A common mistake in informal English is using an object pronoun like "him" instead of a subject pronoun "he."
 
• **Incorrect:** "You are as efficient as him."
 
• **Correct: **"You are as efficient as he is."
 
 
 
• **Rule: Subject Pronoun Use**
 
 
• According to standard grammar rules, when making a comparison where the second clause is implied, the** subject pronoun** must be used because it functions as the subject of an understood verb.

• Mitochondria are **membrane-bound cell organelles **that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions.
 
• Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria is stored in a small molecule called **adenosine triphosphate (ATP).**
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**
 
 
• **Membrane-enclosed organelles **contain an** array of enzymes **capable of breaking down all types of** biological polymers—proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.**

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with building Delhi’s Lāl Quilā (Red Fort)?

• **Lāl Quilā​ **(Red Fort)

 
 
• The** Mughal Emperors' primary residence** was the **Red Fort, also known as Lal Qila, in Old Delhi, Delhi, India**.
 
• When **Shah Jahan chose to move his capital from Agra to Delhi on May 12, 1638, he ordered the Red Fort's construction**.
 
• Its original **colours were red and white**, and architect **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**, who also built the Taj Mahal, is credited with creating it. 
 
• The **fort**, built during Shah Jahan's era, is a prime example of **Mughal architecture and combines Persianate palace design with Indian customs**.
 
• **Nadir Shah's invasion of the Mughal Empire in 1739 **resulted in the **destruction of the fort's artwork and gems**. 
 
• The **fort's defensive walls** sustained little damage, and it was afterwards used as a garrison.
 
• The Indian flag was raised over the** Lahori Gate on August 15, 1947, by Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first prime minister**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every year, the** Prime Minister hoisted the Indian tricolour flag** at the fort's main entrance and delivers a speech from its ramparts on **August 15, which marks India's Independence Day**.
 
• The Red Fort, which is a component of the Red Fort Complex, was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007**.
